extraction_problems: Precise dollar split of independent-expenditure spending between the primary period and the general-election period could not be computed exhaustively (would require reconciling all itemized Schedule E records, including amendments, against exact PA primary election-day boundaries); the primary-vs-general characterization above is based on spot-checking the top committees' itemized records, not a full reconciliation.

OpenFEC's schedules/schedule_e/by_candidate aggregate had not yet incorporated the 2026-08-19 SEED-PAC $11,000 pro-Brooks 24-hour notice at the time of retrieval; it was added to independent_expenditures manually from the itemized schedule_e record rather than the aggregate endpoint.

No FEC financial totals exist for declared candidates Frank Golden, Aiden Alexander Gonzalez, Michael Ramon Granados Jr., and Lewis Shupe (empty results from /candidate/{id}/totals/); their financial fields are null rather than 0, since 'no report filed' is not the same as a confirmed zero.
notes: Coverage_through (2026-06-30) reflects the most recent PERIODIC financial report (FEC Form 3, 'JULY QUARTERLY 2026', filed 2026-07-15) for both major-party nominees' principal committees. As of retrieval (2026-08-30), that is roughly 2 months stale; the next scheduled disclosure is the OCTOBER QUARTERLY report (due on/around 2026-10-15, covering through 2026-09-30).

Both candidates have filed newer non-financial-summary documents since June 30, 2026 (e.g. Brooks filed a Statement of Organization amendment on 2026-08-20; both campaigns have filed periodic 48-Hour Notices of Contributions/Loans around the primary), but these do not update the aggregate receipts/disbursements/cash-on-hand totals shown here.

Bob Brooks (D) won a contested 5-candidate Democratic primary; the other Democratic primary candidates (Ryan Crosswell, Lamont McClure, Carol Obando-Derstine, Mark Pinsley) are not included as candidate entries above because they are not on the 2026 general-election ballot, but their FEC candidate IDs are C00907667/H6PA07162, C00898544/H6PA07147, C00903963/H6PA07154, and C00913947/H6PA07170 respectively, for reference.
Ryan Mackenzie (R) is the incumbent, having defeated then-Rep. Susan Wild (D) in 2024; Wild is not a 2026 candidate (FEC candidate_status = prior-cycle candidate, H8PA15229).

Independent-expenditure totals in 'independent_expenditures' come from OpenFEC's schedules/schedule_e/by_candidate aggregate (deduplicated, i.e. amendments/superseding filings already reconciled), queried for cycle=2026. A naive sum of raw itemized schedule_e line items for these two candidates totals roughly $5.9M, materially higher than the ~$2.76M deduplicated aggregate, because raw itemized records include amended/superseded filings; the deduplicated by_candidate totals are the ones used here.

Spot-checking the underlying itemized Schedule E records for the largest committees (e.g. STRONGER TOGETHER PA supporting Brooks, LEAD LEFT PAC opposing Brooks) shows expenditure dates clustered between 2026-05-06 and 2026-05-18 -- i.e. immediately before Pennsylvania's 2026 primary (inferred to be mid-May 2026 based on FEC 'PRE-PRIMARY 2026' reports covering periods ending 2026-04-29). This strongly suggests the great majority of the ~$2.76M in outside spending found here was primary-season spending (aimed at the multi-candidate Democratic primary), not general-election spending in the Brooks-vs-Mackenzie race. Post-primary (after 2026-05-19) itemized IE activity located for these two candidates was comparatively minor: a handful of small-dollar entries in June 2026 (e.g. Field Team 6 $638.30 and GiveGreen United Action $36.54 supporting Brooks; Planned Parenthood Votes $85.38 opposing Mackenzie) plus one larger, more recent item: an $11,000 pro-Brooks independent expenditure by Seniors Empowering an Effective Democracy (SEED-PAC), reported via a 24-hour notice filed 2026-08-19 (not yet reflected in the by_candidate aggregate; listed separately in independent_expenditures).

No independent expenditures supporting Ryan Mackenzie were found in FEC records as of retrieval; all $12,352.62 in IE activity referencing him was in opposition (mostly small-dollar and primary-period).
No independent expenditure activity was found for the four no-fundraising minor/independent candidates (Golden, Gonzalez, Granados, Shupe).
'Self-funding' = FEC 'candidate_contribution' (candidate's own money loaned/contributed to their committee this cycle), not candidate personal wealth.

'pac_contributions' = FEC 'other_political_committee_contributions' (traditional multicandidate/PAC money); this excludes party-committee contributions and inter-committee transfers, which are called out separately in each candidate's notes field since the fixed schema has no dedicated field for them.
